question.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $R?$

- $(T∨R)∧T$
- $R∧(T∨R)$
- $(R∨T)∧R$
question.worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
R∧(R∨T)≡R.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is *not* logically equivalent to $R.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(T∨R)∧T & ≡T∧(T∨R) \\  & ≡T≢R.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is logically equivalent to $R.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}R∧(T∨R) & ≡R∧(R∨T) \\  & ≡R.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $R.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(R∨T)∧R & ≡R∧(R∨T) \\  & ≡R.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
